reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents Plus Token as a wallet that asks viewers to hold cryptocurrency and activate a feature in exchange for stated recurring returns of 6% to 18% per month, paid daily. It reinforces the promotion with claims of profit from day one, zero-risk arbitrage, possible Ethereum conversion, and later monthly revenue approaching 20%, while directing viewers to Plus Token destinations. The material does not verify the returns or risk characterization, and it contains a tension between the spoken membership-fee statement and the slide's no-fee claim.

citations.quote: how simple it is, in terms of how you can get paid and rewarded to hold your cryptocurrency within the plus token wallet
That's actually the way that they're able to generate revenue for their members
In 2015 they actually created the AI Bot to do crypto arbitrage
So we get rewarded to hold tune of on average six to eighteen percent a month in plus tokens paid daily

opening.argument: Judge the speaker's claims as conditional commentary, not a promise of fixed returns. Even the description of arbitrage limits its risk claim to trades executed properly. The stated reward varies with the coin and trading results, and the speaker attributes the range to what the company has said. A future income strategy is also described as something to be shared later, not demonstrated here. These qualifications matter: an account of proposed performance can be promotional and still fall short of establishing an unconditional guarantee.

citations.quote: where there is zero risk involved as long as trades are executed properly
so depending on the coin and depending on the how well the arbitrage trades go the company has said that they will pay anywhere between 6 to 18% a month
20 refers to a strategy which we will share later with you

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited monthly range is not stated as an invariant result: the speaker ties it to which coin is held and how trades go. Likewise, the risk claim has an express execution condition. The fee tension is a reason to question the presentation's precision, but neither version of the fee claim verifies that returns were paid or establishes a guarantee. The prosecution's evidence supports scrutiny of optimistic claims; it does not by itself settle how literally every forecast should be read.

citations.quote: depending on the coin and depending on the how well the arbitrage trades go
as long as trades are executed properly

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those qualifications do not change the central pitch. The presentation tells viewers that holding cryptocurrency in the wallet and activating AI Dog brings a 6-18% monthly reward paid daily. It also calls arbitrage zero risk and says users are in profit from day one. Conditional wording about trade execution or variation within the range does not supply evidence that the returns or the risk claim are sound.

citations.quote: the company is generating revenue through arbitrage which involves zero risk
you are in profit from day one

opening.argument: This is framed as an overview of a cryptocurrency wallet and how its proposed arbitrage works. The speaker walks through a concrete example of buying on one exchange and selling on another, distinguishes a working wallet from a future project, and identifies an exchange feature as still in beta. That mix of mechanism and product-status detail gives the judge a plausible reading of the video as an explanatory demonstration. The account should be assessed as the speaker's description of the technology, not treated as independent proof that the technology or returns perform as claimed.

citations.quote: This quick video will give you a sort of overview of why plus token, how is it different from other programs out there in the market.

buying of Bitcoin, Ethereum or litecoin or another currency from one exchange where the price is low and then simultaneously selling the same amount of Bitcoin or other cryptocurrency on a different exchange where the price is higher
This is a working model that you can download today, not Tuesday.
The middle screen shows the exchange that's available within the wallet, which is actually currently in beta

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution reads the return claims as the video's whole purpose, but the speaker also devotes attention to wallet screens and distinguishes an available product from a feature still in beta. Its own cited bot explanation describes a mechanism; it does not show trades, payments, or their absence. The description's training link points to more information, while the material here remains an overview rather than a demonstrated transaction.

citations.quote: The middle screen shows the exchange that's available within the wallet, which is actually currently in beta
In 2015 they actually created the AI Bot to do crypto arbitrage
To learn more about how to get paid to HODL, go to our PlusToken Training Website

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Explaining an interface does not make the return pitch incidental. The presentation explicitly connects holding cryptocurrency and activating AI Dog to a 6-18% monthly reward paid daily. The description invites viewers to learn how to get paid to hold. Neither screenshots nor a verbal account of arbitrage verifies the promised performance; they supply a product narrative around the financial inducement.

citations.quote: To learn more about how to get paid to HODL, go to our PlusToken Training Website
That's actually the way that they're able to generate revenue for their members

opening.argument: The narrower reading is promotion of a wallet service, not a request to hand funds to the speaker. The speaker says users hold their own private keys, says there are no packages to buy, and describes withdrawing cryptocurrency from the wallet when needed. Those assertions are not proof of safety, but they matter to what this video actually asks the viewer to do: the material presents use of a purported wallet, without showing a credential request or a transfer to a named recipient. A judge can reject the sales claims without inferring an additional payment mechanism that is not shown.

citations.quote: So the wallet itself is very safe because it's decentralized where you actually hold your own private keys. there are no packages to buy with plus token.
if for whatever reason you need your cryptocurrency back and remove from the wallet you can simply do that. And remove it and withdraw all of your funds. Just like any other wallet.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution points to a fee discrepancy, yet the slide's no-fee claim and the spoken fee wording do not show a completed payment or where users' funds go. The speaker expressly contrasts this service with lending Bitcoin to the company and says users can withdraw. Those are unverified claims, but the evidence offered against them is the promotional presentation itself, not an observed failure to withdraw. Treat the discrepancy as a credibility concern, not proof of a mechanism beyond what is shown.

citations.quote: you are not lending your Bitcoin to the company
And remove it and withdraw all of your funds. Just like any other wallet.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern does not require a visible credential theft or completed transfer. The video promotes placing cryptocurrency in this wallet and activating AI Dog for stated monthly returns paid daily. Claims that users keep their keys or can withdraw do not verify either control of the funds or the return mechanism. The conflicting fee statements further limit how much weight those assurances can bear.
